correctness.rationale: Absolute summability (p≥2) allows grouping the DFT by residues. The wrapped continuous convolution density has Fourier coefficients s_a(j)^p/(2π), yielding the exact normalization and positivity in (1). For circular monotonicity, let r,s≤π be two arc half-lengths and ℓ(x)=max(0,min(2r,2s,r+s−x)) the corresponding line overlap at displacement x≥0. For 0≤d≤π the circular overlap is ℓ(d)+ℓ(2π−d). The second summand can increase only where d>2π−r−s≥|r−s| and d<r+s, hence its increase is canceled by the first summand. Layer cake iterates that monotonicity for all wrapped uniform convolution powers even past later wraps. The minimum is therefore at a nearest-to-π bin, with no uniqueness claim. Strict support yields the ceiling count (2) and the strict thresholds (3), including bins exactly on endpoints. At the nearest bin θ=π−δ_N, the only possible copies in (5) are at θ and θ−2π: other copies have absolute value at least 3π−δ_N, exceeding 5π/4 since δ_N≤π/3. Their signed edge depths are ε+δ_N and ε−δ_N. Positive depths in [0,2a] give the stated density via the volume of a p-dimensional simplex of deficits. Substituting ε=0 and then ε=πt/N gives (4) and (6), including exact zero at each support threshold. These checks reconstruct the universal argument, independent of the finite checker.
correctness.replay: Use absolute convergence to evaluate λ_k by the wrapped density at θ_k. The arc overlap ℓ(d)+ℓ(2π−d) proves all-band monotonicity by layer cake. For α≤π enumerate strict inequalities min(k,N−k)<Nα/(2π). Near wrap compute deficits from ±pa at angles π−δ_N and −π−δ_N; use the simplex density u^(p−1)/((p−1)!(2a)^p) for the first 2a from either edge.
residual_risks: The exact crossover identity has its stated local bandwidth hypotheses; the full spectral representation, but not that local formula, holds at arbitrary bandwidth in scope.
